s: Managed or self-hosted large language model interface for text generation, summarization, classification, and tool-calling.
w: Accepts a prompt (system + user messages) and returns generated text. Models range from small/fast (classification, extraction) to large/reasoning (complex Q&A, code generation). Streaming responses enable token-by-token delivery. Temperature, top-p, and max-tokens control output characteristics. Rate limits, token quotas, and content filters are managed at the API layer.
use: Natural language understanding: sentiment analysis, entity extraction, intent classification
Text generation: content creation, code generation, email drafting
RAG answer generation from retrieved context documents
avoid: Deterministic exact-match tasks (use traditional rules or databases)
Real-time latency-critical paths without caching (LLM inference is 100ms+ per call)
Tasks requiring guaranteed factual accuracy without hallucination mitigation

props.model: Which LLM to invoke (GPT-4, Claude, Llama, etc.)

pat.d: LLM generates answers grounded in retrieved context to reduce hallucination.
LLM decides which tool to call based on user intent; structured output drives actions.

pits: Hallucination in production outputs - implement grounding via RAG and output validation
Token cost explosion from long prompts - trim context, use caching, and set max_tokens
Rate limiting during traffic spikes - implement client-side backoff and request queuing
tips: Temperature and system prompt design are the primary levers for output quality control
Streaming responses improve perceived latency by 3-5x even if total generation time is the same
